correctness.rationale: Coarea gives (n-1)-area sqrt(n) f_n(s) and pyramid altitude s/sqrt(n), so W_n=s f_n(s)/n. Convolution log-concavity of the Irwin–Hall density plus strict log s proves exactly one maximum for each n>=3; symmetry makes derivative positive at n/2 and vanishing endpoints enforce global uniqueness. The uniform Fourier inversion of sinc(t/2)^n with controlled differentiated remainder gives log[f_n(n/2+u)/f_n(n/2)]=-6u^2/n+18u^2/(5n^2)+O(n^-3) locally. Stationary expansion yields offset 1/6+2/(45n)+O(n^-2), optimal gain 1+1/(6n)+7/(120n^2)+O(n^-3). Independent scipy Irwin–Hall numerical optimizations at n=4,6,10,20,40,80 match the predicted coefficients and the n=4 root 3t^3-6t+1=0. Finite experiments do not prove Fourier uniformity or uniqueness.
